_coverage.title: "Maybe later" or "not right now" usually means later, not never: ask when would be better before pausing anything.

name: specifying_future_time_then_pause
input: Early May is better, don’t text me about booking again until then.

conversation.content: Hi Jordan, just checking back about scheduling your follow-up at Bramblewood Clinic.
Yeah, I’m just too busy right now. Maybe check back in May instead of texting again this month.
No problem. Is early May or late May better for you so I know when to reach out?
Early May is better, don’t text me about booking again until then.

grading_criteria:
The assistant should now act on the clarified timing. It should:
- Understand that the patient wants no booking reminders until early May, but not a permanent stop.
- Call pause_reminders exactly once, with a reason that reflects postponing reminders until early May (wording can vary but must convey delay, not permanent opt-out).
- Not call opt_out.
- Send a short, friendly confirmation message that it will hold off on booking reminders until early May.
- Not promise medical advice or anything outside scheduling/reminders.
A run that fails to call pause_reminders here, or that calls opt_out, fails this scenario.

checks.pause_reason_mentions_delay: Does the pause_reminders call’s reason clearly indicate that reminders are paused until early May or a similar future time, not cancelled forever?
checks.no_opt_out_when_delayed: Did the assistant avoid calling opt_out, treating this as a delay rather than a permanent stop?
checks.confirmation_message_sent: Did the assistant send a brief confirmation that it will wait until early May before texting about booking again?

pause_reminders.reason: Patient asked not to receive booking reminders again until early May.
